properties.name: A claim says what its session is doing (working, waiting on a person, blocked, or done), with a checkpoint note the session can revise, and the state's age
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-29, in the dev_reflow2 hub session: "Let's go with your 3 likeliest candidates". Option (a) of dec:idea-a-claim-says-what-its-session-is-doing-and-never-reads-gone-when-it-cannot-be-verified, from the orca and paseo reviews (attention states with a reason; a checkpoint comment beside a phase status).
properties.statement: A claim carries what its session is doing: working, waiting on a person (naming the question it waits on), blocked, or done. It also carries a checkpoint note, which the session can revise while it holds the claim. claim_report and loop_status show both, with the state's age. A state older than the claim's liveness can vouch for reads as unverifiable rather than current, so a stale "working" never reads as true. This is what a dashboard (in flo2's design, req:a-dashboard-page-shows-what-is-being-worked-and-where) would read to show which sessions wait on whom.
